clue.text: They take care a drug's in a compound form

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture made up anew, so these words are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: drug's stands for 'drug is', so the S counts as a letter

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's warning that some medicine comes in a combined preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound form' rearranges A, DRUGS, IN and A (nine letters) into the answer; the possessive-looking 's is really 'is' and gives its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Protectors and legal custodians look after people, so they are the ones who take care.

clue.text: Boldness shown by everybody involved in bridge

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside the other

parts.note: a gantry is a bridge-like frame carrying signals or a crane
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone in a card game shows courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but is a frame over a road or railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and dash in battle is valour or bravery.

clue.text: A good violin is a dull one

parts.note: matt (or mat) means without shine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark that a fine violin can still be a lacklustre one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amati family made violins in Cremona.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments by the Cremona maker family are prized fiddles.

clue.text: The writer made real converts

indicators.note: converts as a verb means changes, so these letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: An author is said to turn fiction into reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' rearranges MADE and REAL; Walter de la Mare was an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and novelist.

clue.text: A misanthrope in no matter what element

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: any means whichever, no matter what
Timon of Athens, in Shakespeare's play, is the famous hater of mankind

explanation.surface: A people-hater who is out of his element in any case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TIMON inside ANY; 'A' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brittle metalloid with symbol Sb is a chemical element.

clue.text: It's bound to happen — unexpectedly

explanation.surface: Something is certain to occur, out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as 'certain', but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a jump forward; to come up suddenly is to appear without warning.

clue.text: The dish featured in one of Goya's pictures

indicators.note: the answer is presented within the run of letters of the words that follow, as a feature appears in a show

explanation.surface: An art note: a plate of food appears in one of the Spanish master's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' signals letters hidden across goyA'S PICtures; 'one of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly set round meat or fish is a cold dish served at table.

clue.text: Attending the big match to demonstrate

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Going to the big game to show support.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness to something is to show it to be true.

clue.text: China appears quite forthright about the alternative church

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, about it

parts.note: plain means frank, quite outspoken
or introduces an alternative
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: China seems blunt about some other church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PLAIN around OR and CE; 'China' looks like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine white ceramic ware is called china.

clue.text: Provision for tea is a help to a sportsman

explanation.surface: Laying on refreshments assists an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea caddy is a small tin for tea leaves; a golfer's caddie (also spelt this way) carries the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tin stores the leaves; a golfer's bag-carrier assists on the course.

clue.text: Circular blade used with constraint

parts.note: a leaf is a flat blade, as of grass or of an oar
let means hindrance, as in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Describes a round saw blade fitted with some restraining guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective for the blade but is a noun, a handbill; LET as an obstruction survives in tennis and in law.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed sheet handed round to many people is called a circular.

clue.text: Dress in a bright colour having finished work

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the dress sitting within the colour

parts.note: red is a vivid hue
tire is an old word for attire, so to dress

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates the end of a career by putting on a vivid outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TIRE (to attire) inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped employment for good, on a pension, has finished working life.

clue.text: A cross on an island that needs no explanation

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Treasure-map talk: X marks the spot on some island, so obvious it needs no comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British island in the Irish Sea; 'on' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth is a statement accepted without proof or justification.

clue.text: Place housing order

parts.note: reads like tidying up a home, but an order here is a religious community of monks, and this is the building where they live

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded instruction to keep a home neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order of monks lives together in a house built for that community.

clue.text: Record circle becoming narrower

parts.note: to tape is to record on tape
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A vinyl disc whose groove spirals ever tighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that thins gradually toward one end grows slimmer along its length.

clue.text: Chief taking standard sum

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
an amount is a sum

explanation.surface: A boss accepting the usual payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme and foremost both mean principal.

clue.text: Found lacking in nobility

explanation.surface: A finding that someone is shown to be without noble qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: To ground or establish something is to base it; mean and ignoble conduct is base.

clue.text: Wind screen set in upright position

indicators.note: to wind is to twist, so these letters are turned into another order

explanation.surface: A car windscreen fitted standing straight up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the breeze that a windscreen blocks, but rearranges SCREEN and SET; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing straight and vertical is being upright.

clue.text: Top musicians get fillet

parts.note: the head is the top
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Leading performers sit down to a cut of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fillet' looks like boneless fish, but is a ribbon worn round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is also a narrow ribbon tied round the hair.

clue.text: He's an expert, but people may well see through him

definitions.text: He's an expert, but people may well see through him

parts.words: He's an expert, but people may well see through him
parts.note: seeing through someone usually means spotting a fraud, but here clients literally see through the lenses this professional prescribes

explanation.surface: A specialist who is not as convincing as he thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesight professional fits spectacles that people look through.

clue.text: Detectives covering 'some distance?

explanation.surface: Police officers on the beat cover quite a lot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, so 'the Yard' means its detectives; 'covering' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yard stands for London's police detectives; three feet make a unit of length.

clue.text: Odd characters press one for an answer

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are odd, that is jumbled, characters

explanation.surface: A phone menu: unusual keys to push to give your reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' rearranges PRESS and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply given to a question or prompt is the same thing as an answer.

clue.text: Coppers after a horse

parts.note: copper coins are pence, abbreviated p
later means after

explanation.surface: Police chasing a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but means pennies; a plater is a poor-quality racehorse, one that runs in selling plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is an inferior racehorse running in minor races for a plate prize.

clue.text: Fast that's right in two ways

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the two road abbreviations

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, another way

explanation.surface: Going without food is correct by two measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' as a verb means go without food; 'in' puts R inside ST and AVE, two roads.
explanation.definitionFit: To go hungry is to fast.

clue.text: About fifty entered, it's concluded

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, about it

parts.note: to enter a race or contest is to compete in it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty people signed up, and the event is now over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'roughly', but it puts COMPETED around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that has been finished is over and done.

clue.text: — is a cad and coward" (Chesterton)

parts.note: a quotation with the gap to fill: G K Chesterton's comic verse insults a hot milky drink as a vulgar beast

explanation.surface: A line of verse from Chesterton abusing a bedtime drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Chesterton's 'Song of Right and Wrong', which praises wine over a hot chocolate drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's poem mocks the chocolate drink in favour of wine and ale.

clue.text: A little place that's not owner-occupied

parts.note: that's is short for 'that is', which gives the word is
a property that is let is rented to tenants rather than lived in by its owner

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note about a small rented property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little place' is a small island; the surface pretends it is a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a small place in the sea.

clue.text: Permission to make a bequest

explanation.surface: A licence to leave property in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is granted permission; to leave property in a will bequeaths it.

clue.text: Opposed to the Bar

explanation.surface: Someone is against the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bar' suggests barristers, but means the serving surface in a pub or shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against means acting contrary; the bar is the long serving top in a pub.

clue.text: A private art-gallery causing disquiet

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
the Tate is the well-known London art gallery

explanation.surface: A privately owned gallery is stirring up unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective but is the soldier; 'causing' is a link, and to disquiet is to unsettle.
explanation.definitionFit: To disquiet someone is to stir up worry and unrest in them.

clue.text: Song about a holy man getting excited

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, about it

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A hymn about some saint gets people worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AIR around ST; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of bustle and commotion means being up and stirred.

clue.text: Compromises offers greens and mash

indicators.note: to mash is to pulp and mix up, so these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A menu that serves vegetables and mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mash' looks like potato but rearranges GREENS and AND; 'offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to put something at risk of harm.
